screening_decisions.reason: Randomized controlled trial in women with urinary stress incontinence. Has three arms including PFMT via digital palpation and a control group with no exercises. Meets all selection criteria.

Randomized controlled trial in women with SUI. The mobile app treatment delivers PFMT (98.4% performed PFMT at follow-up). Control group received postponed treatment (inactive control). Meets all criteria.
Randomized controlled trial in postmenopausal women with SUI. Has PFME (PFMT) alone arm and a control group. Meets all selection criteria.

Randomized placebo-controlled trial in women with urge/mixed incontinence. However, the intervention is 'biofeedback-assisted behavioral treatment' which is not explicitly PFMT. The abstract does not clearly state that pelvic floor muscle training was the intervention component. Does not meet the PFMT criterion.
Randomized controlled trial in women with stress incontinence. Has pelvic muscle exercise (PFMT) arm and control group. Meets all selection criteria.
Randomized controlled trial in women with genuine stress incontinence. Has pelvic floor exercise (PFMT) arm and untreated control group. Meets all selection criteria.
Randomized trial in women with SUI. Has pelvic floor exercise (perineal exercises) arm and control group. Meets all selection criteria.
Randomized controlled trial in women with urodynamic stress urinary incontinence. Has pelvic floor muscle training arm and untreated control group. Meets all selection criteria.
Randomized controlled trial in women with stress and mixed urinary incontinence. Has pelvic floor muscle training arm and control group. Meets all selection criteria.

Randomized controlled trial in women with UI. The behavioral modification program resulted in improved pelvic muscle strength, suggesting PFMT components. Control group had no treatment. Being conservative, include as PFMT elements may be present.

Randomized study in women with stress incontinence. Physical therapy for stress incontinence typically includes PFMT. Abstract is brief but mentions 'medical gymnastics' as most successful. Being conservative, include as PFMT likely included.
Randomized controlled trial in elderly women with SUI. Intervention includes pelvic floor muscle exercises. Has control group. Meets all selection criteria.
Randomized trial in women with stress, urge and mixed UI. Has exercise only arm (includes PFMT) and education group control. Meets all selection criteria.
Randomized controlled trial in women with stress, urge, and mixed UI. Multidimensional exercise treatment includes PFMT components. Has control group. Meets all selection criteria.

Randomized controlled trial in women with stress, urge, or mixed UI. Intervention includes PFMT with manual palpation and verbal feedback. Control received advice and educational pamphlet (inactive control). Meets all selection criteria.
Randomized trial in women with SUI. Has PFMT arm and no treatment control group. Meets all selection criteria.
Randomized trial in women with SUI. Intervention is 'The Knack' - a pelvic floor muscle precontraction technique (PFMT). Has wait-list control. Meets all selection criteria.
Randomized controlled trial in women with SUI. Has PFMT arms (group and individual) and no treatment control group. Meets all selection criteria.
Randomized trial in women with MUI. Has PFMT arm and waiting list control group. Meets all selection criteria.
Randomized controlled trial in women with UI. Physical therapy for UI typically includes PFMT. Control received osteoporosis education (inactive control for UI). Meets all selection criteria.
Randomized trial in women with UI. Has pelvic muscle exercise (PFMT) arm and control group. Meets all selection criteria.
Randomized trial in women with SUI. Has kinesitherapy (physical therapy/PFMT) arm and control group. Meets all selection criteria.
Randomized trial in female athletes with UI. Has PFMRP (pelvic floor muscle rehabilitation program) arm and pamphlet-only control. Meets all selection criteria.
Randomized trial in women with stress incontinence. Has pelvic floor exercises arm and control group. Meets all selection criteria.
Randomized trial in women with genuine stress incontinence. Has pelvic floor exercises arm and no therapy control group. Meets all selection criteria.

RCT in women with stress or mixed UI. One arm received PFM training (3 sets of daily fast and slow contractions). Control arm was untreated with no contact during intervention period. Meets all three selection criteria.

This is a study protocol for an RCT comparing nurse specialist involvement vs usual care in primary care for UI. The intervention is not PFMT specifically, and there is no comparison of PFMT vs inactive control.
RCT assessing consumer satisfaction with nurse specialists vs GPs for UI care. The intervention is not PFMT; this study does not evaluate PFMT as an intervention.

RCT in women with urge/mixed incontinence. One arm received behavioral training with verbal feedback based on vaginal palpation (a form of PFMT). Control arm received self-help booklet (inactive control). Meets selection criteria.
This is a feasibility study, not a randomised controlled trial. While it involves pelvic fitness, the study design does not meet the RCT requirement.
RCT comparing supervised PFMT vs unsupervised PFMT. Both arms receive PFMT; there is no inactive control/no treatment arm. Does not meet criterion 3.

RCT in women with LBP and stress UI. Training group received stabilization exercises focusing on pelvic floor muscle. Control group received routine physiotherapy modalities and regular exercises (active control, not inactive/no treatment).
RCT in women with stress/mixed incontinence. One arm received behavioral training (includes PFMT components). Control arm received self-help booklet (inactive control). Meets all selection criteria.

RCT in elderly women with UI. Training group received Kegel's exercise (PFMT) plus Thera-band training and indoor walking (multicomponent intervention). Control group details not clearly specified as inactive/no treatment. Intervention is not PFMT alone.
RCT comparing behavioral therapy vs no therapy in women with UI. The abstract does not specify that the behavioral therapy includes PFMT. Cannot confirm criterion 2 is met.
Economic evaluation alongside an RCT comparing Internet-based PFMT vs postal PFMT. Both arms receive PFMT; there is no inactive control arm. Does not meet criterion 3.
RCT comparing Internet-based PFMT vs postal PFMT. Both arms receive PFMT training; there is no inactive control/no treatment arm. Does not meet criterion 3.
Long-term follow-up of the same RCT as study 37. Both arms received PFMT; no inactive control arm. Does not meet criterion 3.

RCT in women with SUI. Intervention arm received TA and PFM co-contraction exercise (includes PFMT). Control group mentioned but details not fully specified. Conservative approach: include for full review.
Pilot RCT combining behavioral UI treatments with physical activity (walking and strength training). The intervention is a multicomponent program, not PFMT alone. Does not clearly meet criterion 2.
RCT in gynecological cancer survivors. Intervention was PFMT, but control group received usual health care (active control, not inactive/no treatment). Does not meet criterion 3.
Psychometric validation study of the ICIQ questionnaire. Not a randomised controlled trial. Does not meet criterion 1.
Systematic review of RCTs on conservative treatment of SUI. Not a primary RCT. Does not meet criterion 1.
Systematic review of RCTs on conservative treatment of UUI. Not a primary RCT. Does not meet criterion 1.
Methodological guidance document (CONSORT extension). Not a randomised controlled trial. Does not meet criterion 1.
Review/descriptive article on the impact of UI on self-efficacy and QoL. Not a randomised controlled trial. Does not meet criterion 1.
Psychometric validation study of I-QOL questionnaire across 15 language versions. Not a randomised controlled trial. Does not meet criterion 1.
Instrument development and reproducibility study. Not a randomised controlled trial. Does not meet criterion 1.
Imaging study (MRI) of pelvic floor muscles. Not a randomised controlled trial. Does not meet criterion 1.
Theoretical review article discussing mechanisms of PFMT effectiveness. Not a randomised controlled trial. Does not meet criterion 1.
This is a consensus/terminology report, not a randomised controlled trial. It describes the development of terminology definitions through expert consensus, not an intervention study.
This is a cross-sectional epidemiological survey examining prevalence and burden of UI, not an RCT. No intervention (PFMT) is tested.
This is a review chapter on pathophysiology and pharmacology, not a randomised controlled trial. No PFMT intervention is studied.
This is a review article discussing optimal PFM training regimens and reviewing existing evidence, not a primary RCT testing PFMT vs no treatment.
This study is about functional electrical stimulation (FES), not PFMT. No RCT design comparing PFMT to no treatment is described.
This study involves healthy women (N=38), not women with urinary incontinence. It is not an RCT comparing PFMT to no treatment for UI.
This is a methodological guideline about preparing summary of findings tables, not a clinical trial. No PFMT intervention is studied.
This is a methodological guideline about presenting continuous outcomes in systematic reviews, not a clinical trial. No PFMT intervention is studied.
This is a cross-sectional epidemiological survey assessing prevalence of UI, not an RCT. No intervention is tested.
This is a consensus/terminology report, not a randomised controlled trial. It describes terminology development through expert consensus.
This is a methodological paper about systematic review methodology, not a clinical trial. No PFMT intervention is studied.
This is a cross-sectional study assessing QoL in women with UI, not an RCT. No intervention (PFMT) is tested against no treatment.
This is a systematic review and economic modelling study, not a primary RCT. While it mentions PFMT, it is a review of other trials, not a primary trial itself.
This is a questionnaire development and validation study, not an RCT. No PFMT intervention is tested.
This is an economic study using a willingness-to-pay questionnaire, not an RCT. No PFMT intervention is tested.
This is a cross-sectional analysis examining associations between UI and self-rated health, not an RCT. No intervention is tested.
This is a questionnaire development and validation study, not an RCT. No PFMT intervention is tested.
This is a psychometric validation study for the YIPS scale. Although participants were in a randomized control study, this paper focuses on scale validation, not on testing PFMT vs no treatment.
This is a questionnaire validation study, not an RCT. No PFMT intervention is tested.

This is a methodological paper about trial quality assessment in meta-analyses, not a clinical trial. The trials analyzed were on circulatory, digestive, mental health, and pregnancy topics, not UI/PFMT.
This is a reporting guideline for RCTs, not a clinical trial itself. No PFMT intervention is studied.
This is a cross-sectional survey examining bothersomeness and QoL impact of UI, not an RCT. No intervention is tested.
This is a descriptive study on healthy nulliparous women without urinary incontinence, not an RCT. No intervention comparing PFMT to no treatment is studied.
This is an instrument validation study for a severity index, not an RCT. No PFMT intervention is tested.
This is a cross-sectional study comparing sexual function between incontinent and continent women, not an RCT. No intervention (PFMT) is tested.
Prospective cohort study, not a randomised controlled trial. Also includes both men and women (incontinent adults), not specifically women with UI.
Instrument development/validation study for IIQ and UDI questionnaires. No intervention trial.
Psychometric development study for I-QOL measure. Not an intervention trial.
Study concerns psoriasis patients, not urinary incontinence. Wrong population entirely.
Validation study of Patient Global Impression questionnaires. Secondary analysis of duloxetine trials, not a PFMT intervention trial.
Development of anxiety/depression scale for hospital settings. Not related to urinary incontinence treatment.

Randomized controlled trial in perimenopausal women with stress urinary incontinence. Intervention is pelvic floor muscle exercises. Control group mentioned but nature not fully specified. Includes as conservative decision.
Randomized study in women with stress urinary incontinence. Intervention includes pelvic floor exercises. Control group (GC) mentioned. Unclear if control is inactive, but include conservatively.
RCT but intervention is acupressure, not pelvic floor muscle training. Does not meet PFMT intervention criterion.
RCT comparing home-based vs supervised pelvic floor exercises. Both arms are active PFMT interventions; no no-treatment/placebo/sham control arm.
Randomized controlled trial in women with SUI. Includes PFMT arm and a 'no active treatment' arm. Meets all selection criteria.
Qualitative study (telephone interviews, grounded theory analysis) exploring women's experiences. Not a randomised controlled trial.
Secondary analysis examining predictors of success from a completed RCT. Not a primary intervention trial comparing PFMT to inactive control.
Systematic review comparing PFMT added to other active treatments. Not a primary randomised controlled trial.
Review/overview article compiling 16 articles about PFM exercises. Not a primary randomised controlled trial.
Anatomical/physiological descriptive article about urethrovesical structure. No intervention trial.
Psychiatric symptom inventory validation study. Not related to urinary incontinence treatment.
Chapter/overview of conservative management approaches. Not a primary randomised controlled trial.
Methodological article about trial analysis principles. Not a primary intervention trial.
Systematic review comparing PFMT to other active treatments. Not a primary randomised controlled trial.
Communication about outcome measurement reliability. Not an intervention trial.
Observational cohort study using MRI imaging. Not a randomised controlled trial.
RCT comparing conservative treatment (physiotherapy + bladder retraining) with vs without prior urodynamics. Both arms receive active treatment; no no-treatment/placebo/sham control arm.
Observational clinical and physiologic study of incontinence causes in institutionalized elderly. Not a randomised controlled trial.
Systematic review about PFMT in antenatal and postnatal women. Not a primary randomised controlled trial.
